sections.content: How many people stayed in Ingleby Barwick after gaining qualifications?

Ingleby Barwick is a medium-sized town in the North East. Ingleby Barwick does not have its own university.

Ingleby Barwick has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Ingleby Barwick ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • fewer non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 1,140 state-school pupils from Ingleby Barwick who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 500 (44%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 410 (36%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Ingleby Barwick to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Ingleby Barwick's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Ingleby Barwick in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Ingleby Barwick move to?

Of Ingleby Barwick's graduates, 215 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 80 of those graduates (37%) were living fairly locally, in the Middlesbrough and Stockton travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Ingleby Barwick's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 150 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 100 of those qualified non-graduates (67%) were living fairly locally, in the Middlesbrough and Stockton travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Ingleby Barwick's GCSE cohort:

  • 110 graduates left the North East
  • the most common region they moved to was Yorkshire and The Humber
  • 30 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the North East

In 2018 to 2019, 28% of graduates and 30% of qualified non-graduates living in Ingleby Barwick had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 380 graduates and 365 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Ingleby Barwick. This is compared with the 500 graduates and 410 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 74% of the graduates had also lived in Ingleby Barwick as GCSE pupils, while 28% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Ingleby Barwick in 2018 to 2019, 71% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 30% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
